lead.headline: Gunman kills 6 in Krakow's main square; Poland calls it terrorism
lead.dek: Three relatives found dead at the suspect's home; the interior minister said he was drawn to far-right ideology
body: A gunman firing a military-style rifle from a car killed six people and wounded 15 in Krakow's Main Market Square on Saturday, Polish officials said, and police later found his parents and sister shot dead at his home about 90 miles to the northeast. The dead were four women and two men, a British national among them; Prime Minister Donald Tusk called the attack terrorism.

The suspect, a Polish national in his mid-20s in military-style clothing, was shot by police in an exchange of fire and taken to a hospital in custody, Krakow police said. Interior Minister Marcin Kierwinski said the man "was fascinated by far-right ideologies" and that more weapons were found in his car. Two officers were wounded, one seriously; the injured include citizens of Austria, Britain, Germany, Portugal and Russia.

The National Prosecutor's Office opened a terrorism investigation, AFP reported, and the government declared two days of national mourning from Sunday; Krakow's mayor sealed the square and declared the city in mourning through Wednesday. The U.S. State Department said it knew of no Americans hurt. Mass shootings are rare in Poland.

briefs.headline: Trump says he offered the press secretary job to UFC's Dana White
briefs.summary: Trump posted Saturday that White, "a violent Fighter and Warrior," should bring UFC fighters as assistants; White said he will meet Trump Monday. The post has been empty since Katie Zacharia left after five days in October.

briefs.headline: Judge names special master to probe answers in Trump golf course case
briefs.summary: U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes said Saturday she intends to appoint former U.S. attorney Jessie Liu to examine whether Interior, Park Service and DOJ lawyers misled her about the East Potomac renovation, which closes the course Nov. 15.

briefs.headline: Trump orders DOJ to 'look into' Democrats' impeachment threats
briefs.summary: Trump wrote on Truth Social Saturday that Democrats threatening his cabinet members with impeachment amounted to "extortion at the highest level"; he offered no evidence and the department made no comment.

briefs.headline: Colom leads by 2,574 as Mississippi counts through the weekend
briefs.summary: AP's count at 5 p.m. Friday had Colom ahead of Hyde-Smith with thousands of affidavit ballots left; Rankin County has rejected about 20% of those it processed, mostly for wrong precincts. Mail ballots are due Tuesday; counties certify Friday.

briefs.headline: Herzog gives Eisenkot first chance to form Israel's government
briefs.summary: The president told the former army chief Saturday night; 67 lawmakers recommended him to Netanyahu's 46, and he has 28 days to reach 61 seats. Netanyahu said a coalition "dependent on Islamists" would dismantle the state from within.

briefs.headline: French protests draw 146,000 on a 4th weekend; Lecornu meets unions Monday
briefs.summary: The Interior Ministry counted 146,000 nationwide and 46,000 in Paris, unions 250,000; police used tear gas at Place de la Nation and in Lyon, and two Yellow Vest leaders were arrested. Students plan a new strike Tuesday.

briefs.headline: Magnitude 5.7 quake injures more than 20 in central Japan
briefs.summary: The quake struck western Shizuoka at 1:04 a.m. Sunday at a depth of about 40 km, Kyodo reported; no tsunami warning was issued, Tokaido Shinkansen trains were delayed and the weather agency saw no change in the Nankai Trough.

briefs.headline: Zelenskyy says Ukraine downed 4 of 36 Russian missiles overnight
briefs.summary: He said Saturday the shortfall shows an interceptor shortage, that 172 drones also struck 13 regions, and that one site showed North Korean KN-23 missiles. Russian, Ukrainian and U.S. negotiators meet Tuesday in Abu Dhabi.

briefs.headline: Ripley High athletic director jailed on four felony counts
briefs.summary: Deputies arrested Steven Lough, 56, at Friday's football game on three counts of sexual contact with a student and one obscene-matter count; Jackson County Schools cut ties Nov. 6.

briefs.headline: PSC approves Mountaineer Gas settlement worth $17.3M a year
briefs.summary: Base rates rise about $17.3 million a year for 220,000 customers, partly offset by a lower infrastructure charge; the usage rate could go up in December, MetroNews reported Saturday.

briefs.headline: Ruby Memorial employee sues over hidden restroom cameras
briefs.summary: One of eight employees recorded in a staff restroom sued WVU Hospitals and a former anesthesiologist Friday in Monongalia Circuit Court; two nurses filed similar suits Nov. 3.

briefs.headline: Marshall medical school gets $15M for simulation center
briefs.summary: HHS awarded the Joan C. Edwards School of Medicine $15 million for a center to train medical, nursing and pharmacy students, the Herald-Dispatch reported Saturday; Capito requested it.

regional.item: A Mountaineer Gas line ruptured near Casto Road in Mason County on Saturday evening; emergency management later said it was contained.
Two people died in an apparent murder-suicide at a Clay Avenue home on Charleston's West Side on Saturday, police said.
The I-77 northbound on-ramp at Exit 174 in Wood County closes Nov. 12 and the off-ramp Nov. 13, 7 a.m. to 3 p.m., for guardrail work.
The Hinton Area Foundation funded 12 projects in its fall grant round, WVVA reported Friday, eight of them in Summers County classrooms.

away.item: A Pownal man pleaded guilty Nov. 3 in Bennington Superior Court to aggravated assault in a neighbor-dispute shooting and to deer poaching.

hotspots.item: WVSSAC's official Class A pairings Saturday sent No. 13 Webster County (6-4) to No. 4 East Hardy (9-1); first-round dates and times come Sunday.
A quorum of North Topsail Beach's aldermen will attend a strategic planning workshop at Town Hall at 10 a.m. Monday, the town posted Nov. 6.

briefs.headline: Windstorm cuts power to 13,878 customers around Prince George
briefs.summary: BC Hydro said 13,878 central Interior customers were still out Saturday morning, down from a provincial peak of about 80,000 Friday, and that it is tracking two and likely three more systems through midweek.

briefs.headline: Island storm drops 200 mm of rain, cancels evening ferries
briefs.summary: The season's first storm dumped more than 200 mm on much of Vancouver Island, Global News reported, with 40,000 BC Hydro customers dark at 8 a.m. Saturday. BC Ferries cancelled two evening Swartz Bay sailings; a third storm is due Monday.

briefs.headline: Champagne defends budget as debt interest tops health transfers
briefs.summary: Finance Minister Francois-Philippe Champagne told CTV News "deficits are lower, that's a fact." The budget projects $60.2B in debt interest next year against $57.4B in health transfers, and a deficit above $62B.

briefs.headline: Alberta puts physician triage teams in six emergency rooms
briefs.summary: Premier Danielle Smith said Saturday the teams are now working in six ERs. The province announced the plan in January after Prashant Sreekumar, 44, died following a nearly eight-hour wait at an Edmonton hospital.

briefs.headline: Unifor reads Stellantis silence as proof Brampton plant is sold
briefs.summary: Stellantis would neither confirm nor deny a sale to armoured-vehicle maker Roshel when it met the union Friday, Unifor said; a company spokesperson said it had "nothing to announce." The plant has been idle since 2023.

briefs.headline: NASA picks 8 companies for $10B Moon Base cargo contract
briefs.summary: Blue Origin, SpaceX, Firefly and five others will compete for lunar deliveries under the 10-year contract, NASA said Saturday. Blue Origin also received $94M to land a nuclear-powered rover at the south pole in late 2028.

briefs.headline: Early heart procedures add no survival benefit over 13 years
briefs.summary: ISCHEMIA-EXTEND followed more than 5,000 stable coronary disease patients for up to 13 years and found 26% died after early invasive treatment against 27% on drugs alone, NYU Langone reported in JAMA.

briefs.headline: Heavy rain more than doubled an Alaska glacier's speed
briefs.summary: GPS fixes every 15 seconds on Turner Glacier showed 20 mm of rain during its 2020-21 surge sped the ice up 116% within about 12 hours, Boise State researchers reported in The Cryosphere.

briefs.headline: Polar vortex breakdown forecast weeks earlier than any on record
briefs.summary: ECMWF scientists said the stratospheric vortex disruption is likely the earliest observed, with a full breakdown forecast by Nov. 20. A November warming had occurred only three times since the 1950s, each on Nov. 28.

briefs.headline: Best coding agent fully completes 26% of real user requests
briefs.summary: On Co-Design Bench, 273 change requests drawn from real coding sessions, OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra met 69.9% of acceptance criteria but fully finished 26.4% of tasks, researchers at Alibaba and partner universities reported.

briefs.headline: Nine AI agents fail every open science task set by DOE labs
briefs.summary: Given 15 follow-up problems from Energy Department lab scientists, agents from OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek and others wrote 135 papers; none met every condition and 114 failed an integrity check, a Carnegie Mellon-led team said in an October paper.

briefs.headline: Bank of England puts AI's productivity lift at 0.5% over 3 years
briefs.summary: The bank's November Monetary Policy Report, out this week, found AI added 0.1 to 0.2 points to annual productivity growth since early 2024, and that surveyed firms report virtually no employment effect so far.

weather_ear: Sunday's sky and temperature come at 7:15, from the weather desk.
kicker: Nicholas-Webster carries no regional line today; Summers-New River files for the first time in a week.

art.caption: Krakow's Main Market Square, nearly empty, with the Cloth Hall across the far side and two officers and a passerby on the cobbles.
